key_insight: The paper develops an ALE finite-volume solver for relativistic detonation waves that preserves the inert conservation-law structure while adding reaction physics through an extra energy term and reactant equation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical high-order numerical tool for simulating strong relativistic combustion/shock interactions, with potential relevance to astrophysical explosion modeling and energy-release predictions.
method: Second-order ALE finite-volume scheme with TVD reconstruction and mesh velocity matched to the shock speed.
Locally implicit treatment of stiff reaction source terms in the reactant evolution equation.
Efficient conserved-to-primitive variable conversion tailored to relativistic Euler equations.
evidence_signal: The solver successfully reproduces the Zel'dovich-von Neumann-Doering detonation profile up to shock Lorentz factors of about 7 and reveals a non-monotonic relativistic pressure-jump behavior.
watch_item: Accuracy and robustness depend on shock-tracking mesh motion and a delicate conserved-to-primitive inversion, so performance may degrade in more complex multi-dimensional or highly stiff regimes.
paper_title: An Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian solver for relativistic detonation waves
